# Preface {.unnumbered}

## About this tutorial

This tutorial outlines some key statistical methods needed to analyze randomized controlled trials (RCTs), as conducted in our hands-on RCT courses (@zurich), as well as tools in R to do these methods in practice:

- B102 ("Konzepte und Methoden der Epidemiologie") in the Master of Public Health program,
- BME361 ("Randomised trials – From lab experiments to large preventive trials") in the MSc program in Biomedicine, and 
- EPI301 ("Introduction to Epidemiology") in the PhD programs in Epidemiology and Biostatistics; Clinical Science; and Care & Rehabilitation Science.

There are many potential study designs (e.g. two-arm parallel group, more than 2 parallel groups, crossover trials, cluster-randomized, case-control, ...) and types of outcomes (e.g. continuous normally-distributed, continuous but not normal, binary, ordinal, categorical, survival). We focus on performing the following key steps in analyzing a medical study:

- summarizing binary and continuous outcomes,
- comparing these outcomes in a two-sample setting, and
- analyzing such a study using R.

Along the way, we'll cover p-values, confidence intervals, and choice of statistical method for the most basic of RCTs. We do not aim to provide a comprehensive overview to statistical methodology, but to get you started with some methods that are applicable in many common situations. For more information on these topics, try these resources for statistical methods:

- *Essential Medical Statistics* @kirkwood
- *Medizinische Statistik*: @held
- the online script for the [*Clinical Biostatistics*](https://bookdown.org/charlotte_micheloud93/Clinical_Biostatistics/) course
- *Statistical Issues in Drug Development*: @senn
- *Cross‐over Trials In Clinical Research*: @crossover

and R programming:

- *Hands-On Programming with R*: @hopr
- *R for Data Science*: @r4ds
- *ggplot2: Elegant Graphics for Data Analysis*: @ggplotbook

*This tutorial is a work in progress! Please contact me at [sarah.haile@uzh.ch](mailto:sarah.haile@uzh.ch) if you have any comments or questions. Or file a bug report on [github](https://github.com/srhaile/epi_teaching/issues).*
